summary:
H.R. 8752, the "Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2025," appropriates funds for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) for fiscal year 2025, ending September 30, 2025. The bill is organized in five titles, each addressing a functional grouping of DHS components, and includes numerous administrative provisions, general provisions, and rescissions.

**Title I** appropriates funds for Departmental Management, Intelligence, Situational Awareness, and Oversight, including the Office of the Secretary and Executive Management, the Management Directorate, the Office of Intelligence and Analysis, and the Office of Inspector General. Section 101 requires the Secretary to report all non-competitive grants and contracts from FY2024–2025 to the Inspector General by October 15, 2025, with IG review due to the Appropriations Committees by February 15, 2026. Section 102 mandates monthly budget and staffing reports from the Chief Financial Officer. Section 103 conditions transfers from the Treasury Forfeiture Fund (31 U.S.C. 9705(g)(4)(B)) on prior notification to the Appropriations Committees. Sections 105 and 106 impose quarterly acquisition briefing requirements and pilot program documentation and reporting obligations, respectively.

**Title II** appropriates funds for U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), the Coast Guard, and the U.S. Secret Service. Section 211 earmarks $1,390,338,000 for CBP procurement with specified allocations including $600,000,000 for physical barriers, requiring steel bollard pedestrian barriers of 18–30 feet effective height with anti-climb and anti-dig features at locations identified in the August 1, 2020 Border Security Improvement Plan, with obligation required within 120 days of enactment. Section 212 prohibits dismantling existing U.S.–Mexico barriers unless simultaneously repaired or replaced. Section 213 bars use of the CBP One application to facilitate parole. Sections 218–219 address section 287(g) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1357(g)) delegations, prohibiting reduction in participation except where the IG determines material breach. Section 220 bars continuation of detention contracts with facilities receiving two consecutive sub-adequate performance evaluations. Section 228 requires ICE to maintain detention at full facility capacity and mandate GPS monitoring for all non-detained docket aliens. Sections 225, 226, 227, 230, 231, and 232 impose restrictions on interior transport, abortion funding, gender-affirming care, alien identification cards, Alternatives to Detention standards, and protected-area enforcement guidelines, respectively. Sections 250–251 prohibit TRICARE cost-sharing for contraceptives for Coast Guard members and dependents, effective 30 and 180 days post-enactment, respectively.

**Title III** appropriates funds for the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), and the National Flood Insurance Fund. Section 302 raises the administrative cost cap to 5 percent for specified grant programs. Section 304 imposes a $1,000,000 rescission penalty for premature public grant announcements. The Disaster Relief Fund receives $22,741,000,000, designated as disaster relief under section 251(b)(2)(D) of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985.

**Title IV** appropriates funds for U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers, the Science and Technology Directorate, and the Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction Office. Section 406 authorizes the Secretary to increase H-2B visa numbers above the statutory cap (8 U.S.C. 1184(g)(1)(B)) by the highest returning-worker participation level. Section 408 bars H-1B petition approval for entities identified under section 1260H of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for FY2021.

**Title V** contains general provisions. Section 503 establishes reprogramming and transfer notification requirements with specified thresholds and a June 15 cutoff. Section 507 mandates advance notification for grants, contracts, and awards exceeding specified amounts. Section 527 guarantees Members of Congress and designated employees access to DHS detention facilities without prior notice. Section 528 restricts restraints on pregnant detainees. Sections 536 and 537 prohibit funding to entities identified under section 1260H and transfer of Guantanamo detainees, respectively. Section 538 requires bimonthly southwest border arrival estimates, with suspension of reprogramming authority for noncompliance. Sections 543–567 impose numerous policy riders, including prohibitions on the Circumvention of Lawful Pathways rule, Disinformation Governance Board, classification of speech as mis- or disinformation, implementation of specified Executive Orders, the Public Charge rule, electric vehicle purchases, COVID-19 mask mandates, environmental justice strategies, Safe Mobility Offices, and the salary of the Secretary of Homeland Security. Sections 550–551 rescind $600,000,000 from CBP barrier construction balances (Public Law 116-260) and $154,000,000 from the DHS Nonrecurring Expenses Fund. Section 553 prohibits reduction of operating hours at 15 specified northern border ports of entry.
